description: This is a LIBRARY, not a deployable. It has no Dockerfile and no chart,
so the per-platform base-image care that go-service-template's config
needs does not apply here. What does apply: every dependency bump landing
here propagates to every service built on the kit the moment they bump
the kit, so grouping and reviewability matter more than speed.
PLATFORM NOTE: the homelab Renovate instance runs against gitlab.orac.local
with autodiscover on, so it will open MRs on the GitLab dev remote, not on
GitHub. GitHub carries the canonical module path, so a merged Renovate MR
is not visible to consumers until main is pushed to the github remote and
a new tag is cut. Merging on GitLab alone changes nothing for anyone.
DO NOT let Renovate touch the go directive. Its gomod manager will
raise 'go 1.26.0' to whatever patch release is current, and that is a
build-breaking change here rather than a routine bump: the standard
golang:1.26 CI image ships some patch of its own, and with
GOTOOLCHAIN=local a directive newer than the image is a hard failure --
go: go.mod requires go >= 1.26.5 (running go 1.26.4)
which is invisible locally and only fails in CI.
This already shipped once: v0.1.0 was tagged with 'go 1.26.5' and could
not be built by the homelab pipeline at all. See CHANGELOG 0.1.1.
Go version changes are a deliberate human decision. Raising the
LANGUAGE version (1.26 -> 1.27) is a compatibility decision that wants
a human anyway; raising the PATCH is never something this file should
want. go-service-template's e2e harness has a check that fails on a
patch-pinned directive; there is no equivalent guard here, so the rule
below is the only thing holding the line.
OpenTelemetry moves as a release train: the SDK, the API, the
exporters and the contrib instrumentation are only tested together, and
a partial bump produces a module graph that compiles and then fails at
runtime on a version mismatch. One grouped PR or none.
The kit is where OTel actually lives, so this is the single most
consequential rule in this file. A bump can also RENAME metrics --
the semconv import is pinned in exactly one file (obs/obs.go) for this
reason -- which breaks dashboards downstream. Read the OTel release
notes before merging, and re-check the metric names recorded in
obs.RuntimeMetricNames.
huma is the API layer for every service built on this kit, and its
observable behavior is pinned by tests here (422 rather than 400 for
validation failures, an absent problem+json 'type' member). Review it
on its own so a behavior change is not buried in a batch.
GitHub Actions: one grouped PR for the whole workflow set. Low risk
individually, high noise in aggregate.
